outcome: Maternal complications (prolonged labor, postpartum hemorrhage, shoulder dystocia)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies with a birth weight equal to or exceeding 4000 g at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at GIMSR Teaching Hospital, from May 2018 to May 2023.
finding: The prevalence of macrosomia was 3.86%, and the main risk factors were male gender, pre-pregnancy BMI >25, previous macrosomic births, and excessive weight gain during pregnancy.
